quote: We hold these truths to be self-evident, that all men are created equal...
context: From the Declaration of Independence, 1776 -- Jefferson drew heavily on Enlightenment philosophers like John Locke for the framing.

quote: Give me liberty, or give me death!
context: Delivered at the Virginia Convention, March 1775 -- no verbatim transcript survives; the text was reconstructed decades later from listeners' memories.

quote: I only regret that I have but one life to lose for my country.
context: Said before his execution as a spy by the British in 1776, at age 21 -- like Henry's line, the exact wording is not independently verified.

quote: These are the times that try men's souls.
context: Opens 'The American Crisis,' 1776 -- Washington had it read aloud to his freezing, demoralized troops before crossing the Delaware.

quote: Government of the people, by the people, for the people, shall not perish from the earth.
context: Closing line of the Gettysburg Address, November 1863 -- the entire speech runs only about 272 words.

quote: I have a dream that my four little children will one day live in a nation where they will not be judged by the color of their skin.
context: Delivered at the March on Washington, August 28, 1963 -- King departed from his prepared text for much of the 'I have a dream' section.

quote: Ask not what your country can do for you — ask what you can do for your country.
The only thing we have to fear is fear itself.
context: From FDR's first inaugural address, March 1933, delivered at the depth of the Great Depression.

quote: Fourscore and seven years ago our fathers brought forth on this continent, a new nation...
context: 'Fourscore and seven' means 87 years -- counting back from 1863 lands on 1776, tying the speech directly to the Declaration.

quote: United we stand, divided we fall.
context: The line 'by uniting we stand, by dividing we fall' comes from Dickinson's 1768 song 'The Liberty Song' -- one of the first American patriotic songs, predating the Declaration by 8 years.
